name: git_status
description: Read-only snapshot of the working tree's state relative to the last commit: current branch, and which files are staged, unstaged, or untracked. The tool to call before any operation that could discard or overwrite uncommitted work.

cwd.description: Directory to run the status check from, relative to the workspace root. Must resolve inside a git repository.

include_untracked.description: Report untracked files. Disabling this answers a narrower question — 'is anything tracked modified' — and must not be used to make a dirty tree look clean.

branch.description: Current branch name, or a detached-HEAD commit reference.

staged.description: Files staged for the next commit.

untracked.description: Files git does not yet track. Empty if `include_untracked` was false, not because none exist.

clean.description: True only when `staged`, `unstaged`, and (if requested) `untracked` are all empty. A tree is never reported clean while `include_untracked` is false and untracked files might exist — see `safety_notes`.

ahead.description: Commits ahead of the upstream branch, if one is configured.

behind.description: Commits behind the upstream branch, if one is configured.

errors.description: `cwd` does not resolve inside a git repository.
`cwd` resolves outside the workspace root and was refused before any git command ran.

safety_notes: Strictly read-only — this tool runs no command that stages, commits, stashes, or discards anything. `clean` is defined precisely so it cannot be misread as a green light: when `include_untracked` is false, `clean` reflects tracked files only and must be reported to a human alongside that caveat, never presented bare as 'nothing to lose.' This is the tool `skills/git.md` requires calling before any destructive git operation, and its result should be re-checked immediately before that operation runs, not cached from an earlier point in a session — the tree can change between the check and the act.
